full_judgment:
2. Facts essential to dispose the appeals are that Md. Nurul Miah, predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos.1(a)-(g) and Bazlu Miah, predecessor-in-interest of respondent No.2(a), as pre-emptors filed Miscellaneous Case Nos.3 and 4 of 1991 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Shahrasti, Chandpur under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act, 1950) for per-emption of the respective case land transferred to the pre-emptee appellant herein (in both appeals) by kabalas dated 20.01.1990, 21.01.1990 respectively. 

 "Mr. A.K. Badrul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in both the petitions submits that though land of cadastral Survey Khatian Nos.18-21 had been shown as tenanted land in the sale deed dated 17.04.1926 under Cadastral Survey Khatian No.17 but the said under tenancies subsequently got no existence as under tenancies and the said land went to khan holding of Cadastral Survey Khatian No.17 and those land of under tenancies stood recorded in State Acquisition Khatian No.10 in the names of tenants or heirs of transferors Cadastral Survey Khatian No.17 and not in the names of heirs of any under tenants of Cadastral Survey Khatian Nos.18-21 and the deed of conveyance dated 17.04.1926 is a positive proof that Karim Uddin and his three (3) brothers purchased 3.76 acres of land from sons of Yakub Ali and Karim Uddin got. 94 acres of land in the case holding and pre-emptor-petitioner inherited .18-2 acres of land from his holding and father Karimuddin and pre-emptor petitioner still remains owner and co-sharer by way of inheritance in respect of li acres of land after transfer of .17 acres of land and pre-emptor petitioner having been a co sharer by way of inheritance, pre-emption cases by pre-emptor respondent is not at all maintain-able and both the trial Court and the Lower Appellate Court concurrently found that the pre-emptor petitioner is a co-sharer by inheritance and those findings rested upon correct construction and reading of the sale deed dated 17.04.1926, share of Yukub Ali in the case holding and materials on record but the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division totally misdirected himself in his approach in resolving the legal battle involved in pre-emption cases and committed a substantial error in holding that pre-emptor-petitioner inherited .13 acres of land and transferred .17 acres of land and thereby exhausted all his interest in case holding and became a stranger and this Division did not at all explore the legal controversy and in a summary way dismissed the leave petitions and judgment under challenge in Civil Review Petition may kindly be reviewed in the interest of justice. 

 Mr. Huq submits that the pre-emptor-respondent-side in Mutation and sub Division of Joint Tenancy and holding case Nos.303 of 1987-1988 and 296 of 1987-1988 got Joint Tenancy and Holding i.e. State Acquisition Khatian No.10 separated and sub division and got their names mutated in separate Khatians in respect of 4.13 acres respectively and predecessor vendors of per-emptee-petitioner Shasuddin and others in Mutation and Sub Division of Holding Case No.301 of 1987-1988 got their Holding Sub-division and separated on opening of new Khatian in respect of 2.18 acres of land and the original Joint Tenancy and holding i.e. State Acquisition Khatian No.10 gat no existence and pre-emptor respondent side and predecessor vendors of pre-emptor-petitioner who stepped in to shoes of predecessor vendor-respondents, no longer remained co-sharer of the transferred holding and the pre-emptor respondent side ceased to be co-sharer of the tenancy and holding i.e. State Acquisition Khatian No.10, and thus, had legal character and locus standi to exercise right of Pre-emption against Pre-emptee petitioner and though the learned Trial Court Judge and the Appellate Court Judge took into stock this fundamental aspect of the matter neither the High Court Division nor the Appellate Division took into consideration the same and ruminated the vital and core legal aspect of the matter and that in the event of consideration and meditation of this important aspect of the matter, the fate of Civil Revisions and Civil Petitions For Leave to Appeal would have been otherwise and Per-petitioner would have been graced with favorable verdict and, as such impugned judgment may kindly be reviewed to secure ends of justice."
